sentences.text: Utatsusaurus possessed a slender body that measured nearly 2.5 to 3 meters in length and weighed approximately 57.8 kilograms.
This early relative of modern ichthyosaurs lacked a dorsal fin and featured a broad skull with small teeth arranged in a primitive groove.
Its limb proportions were distinct, showing humeri and femurs of equal length while the hindlimbs appeared larger than the forelimbs.
The animal had small fins containing five digits, some of which could possess up to five extra finger bones in a condition known as hyperphalangy.
Later detailed examination of the holotype revealed that the teeth were more robust and blunt-pointed than originally described.
Utatsusaurus holds the distinction of being the earliest known ichthyopterygian, living during the Early Triassic period approximately 245 to 250 million years ago.
Its long, low tail fin suggests it swam by undulation rather than using paddles and a fluked tail.
The first specimen was discovered in Utatsu-cho, now part of Minamisanriku-cho, in Miyagi Prefecture, Japan.
Ryosuke Motani, Nachio Minoura, and Tatsuro Ando re-examined the fossils in 1998 using computer imagery to correct skeletal distortion.
The museum housing these fossils, the Gyoryū-kan, was destroyed on March 11, 2011, during the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami.
Fossil evidence indicates that Utatsusaurus fed on a diet of fish.
The animal possessed approximately 40 cylindrical presacral vertebrae, suggesting it swam with an eel-like motion.
Anatomy shows that Utatsusaurus possessed transitional features between ancestral terrestrial amniotes and more derived ichthyosaurs.
The genus belongs to the family Utatsusauridae.
Shikama, Kamei, and Murata named the genus Utatsusaurus and the species Utatsusaurus hataii in 1978, making the latter the type species.
Taxonomically, Utatsusaurus is classified as a reptile.
Phylogenetic analyses concluded that ichthyosaurs are members of Diapsida and the sister group of Sauria, with Utatsusaurus forming a basal clade with Parvinatator.
Researchers found Utatsusaurus closely related to lizard-like diapsid reptiles like Petrolacosaurus, making ichthyopterygians distant relatives of lizards, snakes, and crocodiles.
A specimen assigned to cf. Utatsusaurus hataii was found in the Lower Triassic Osawa Formation in Japan.
